subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw change memory_search chunking to respect Markdown headings by default, add an opt-in chunking strategy/config, or defer chunking until the broader Memory MVP/entity design is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation changes persisted index identity and user retrieval behavior, and the issue also bundles a larger entity/graph-memory direction that needs product ownership.

options.title: Split and approve a narrow chunking design
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

options.title: Make heading-aware default
options.body: Adopt heading boundaries as the canonical chunking behavior for Markdown memory files, accepting that existing headed files will reindex and retrieve differently.

options.title: Defer to Memory MVP design
options.body: Keep this open but wait for the memory write/entity pipeline decisions so chunking, extraction, and wiki synthesis land as one coordinated design.

recommendation.title: Split and approve a narrow chunking design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The core memory chunking, config, and index identity boundary is the immediate product/API decision point.
